decision: The source is a fictional saved page. Its published wording and displayed request link support a partner copy proof. A working destination, finished design and owner template approval are pending.

deck.detail: All three PDF pages read as text and inspected as full slides and a thumbnail strip. The deck is team material. Public copy below uses independent website clearance.

website.detail: Read the saved source, rendered its content offline and checked the method, action text, CSS and href. No destination capture or submission receipt was supplied.

conflicts.issue: Instant download in the retired handout versus enquiry and email reply on the saved public page.
conflicts.decision: Use the newer public service-page wording: the manager sends an enquiry and a coordinator emails a sample. No response time or immediate download. A working form was not independently established.

conflicts.issue: A restricted pilot contains a named branch and throughput figures; the partner may use the published identity and public page.
conflicts.decision: Keep the branch, all counts and the pilot notes inside the team. Make no speed or throughput claim. Use the public endpoint limit.

voice.rule: Use a specific floor action. The site says “Record both ends.” Name the unit, numbers and record.
voice.after: Before packing, we record the first and last call numbers of each shelf run on the route sheet.

voice.rule: Keep the sequence and recipient intact. “After shelving” starts the comparison; a mismatch has a named audience and a time.
voice.before: Our quality check catches issues at delivery.
voice.after: After shelving, we compare those two numbers with the sheet. We flag a mismatch for the collections manager before the run reopens.

voice.rule: State the boundary near the method. The service page limits the check to endpoints.
voice.before: Every volume lands in the right place.
voice.after: We check the two endpoints of each shelf run.

voice.rule: Write the exchange in order. Say “enquiry” for the manager’s action and “replies by email” for the coordinator’s.
voice.after: Send an enquiry. A coordinator will email a route-sheet sample.

visual.rule: Use ink #142F38 for copy, paper #FAF6E9 for the page and action #864018 for the CTA fill, small process labels and thin rules. Set CTA text in paper.

Use Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif for the headline and headings, with Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif for body and the request. The public hero is large, left aligned and limited to 14ch. The page body uses 1.55 line height.

The website header sets ASTER QUIRE in bold uppercase live text. Use that wording in a single line, uncondensed and unrotated; it is a temporary wordmark. There is no approved artwork, intrinsic logo ratio or official clear-space rule on file.
The page assigns 01 / RECORD and 02 / READ BACK to different actions and separates them with whitespace. Its last section has one filled request link below the explanation.

The deck cover uses a single 33 pt Times-Bold title. Each body slide has a thin header rule, a compact identifier and large empty areas. The slide 2 stage labels remain spatially distinct in miniature. The deck’s retired CTA appears only as quoted copy.

For Letter print, allow 0.65 in outer margins; start with a 34–40 pt headline, 18–22 pt stage headings, 11–13 pt body, and at least 10 pt for the printed URL. Put a line of clear space above and below the live-text wordmark. Allow one or two body lines per stage; wrap for legibility.

Use two distinct 24 × 24 unfilled, round-ended line icons, approximately 1.7–2 units wide. A sheet with lines means record; a magnifier means compare. Keep the numbered labels with them. The icons are new editorial illustrations, not logo assets.

Read down one column: promise, scope, record, read back, enquiry. Align the two actions on a slim vertical rule so a reader sees one route sheet checked twice. Use the same first/last pair in both stages if shown. No invented call numbers or client examples are necessary.

sheet.headline: Keep the shelf run readable.
sheet.intro: Planning a branch move? Our check covers only the two endpoints of each open-shelf run.

cards.label: 01 / Record both ends
cards.text: Before packing, we write the first and last call numbers of each shelf run on the route sheet.

cards.label: 02 / Read both ends back
cards.text: After shelving, we compare both numbers with the sheet. We flag a mismatch for the collections manager before the run reopens.

sheet.action_note: Send an enquiry. A coordinator replies by email with the sample.

production.direction: Make an editable US Letter portrait one-sheet, 8.5 × 11 in, plus a single-page print PDF. This is a proposed format. Start with the live-text wordmark and one serif headline. Follow with the scope, two vertically ordered actions, then a single request and a printable destination. No finished reference was supplied.
production.relationship: The team records one pair of endpoints before packing and compares the same pair after shelving. Show those actions in one vertical sequence, using a record-sheet icon for the first stage and a comparison magnifier for the second. Keep exception handling with the second action.
production.assets: Use the approved website wording, colors and local type stacks supplied here. Use the live-text name and new simple line icons as editable shapes. No master logo, licensed font files, photos or reference composition were supplied. Keep the name in its natural proportions.
production.acceptance: V1: at reading size the check is limited to endpoints, the mismatch reaches the collections manager before reopening, and the sample follows an enquiry and email reply. V2: at thumbnail size the headline leads, 01 and 02 form a visible sequence with different icon silhouettes, and a single CTA follows. V3: hide both stage paragraphs; the two labels, symbols and CTA should still identify record, read back and request. Restore the copy and verify all qualifications and a legible printed URL.
